category_title: High-ability students who adopt effective self-testing and practice strategies
minimal_context: The student is responding to an open-ended prompt in an online LMS about future study plans for an introductory algebra course.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please respond to the open-ended prompt in the training module regarding your future study plans and strategy selection for the introductory algebra course.

STUDENT: If I were studying for an exam I would only use Self-testing and I would use practice quizzes to also help me with that.

TUTOR: Are there any other materials in the LMS you plan to use?

STUDENT: Maybe the study guides, but I'll probably just look at them right before the test. I'm not really focused on this initial attempt.

TUTOR: Please go ahead and complete the rest of the current algebra module.

STUDENT: (Clicks rapidly through the module without reading) I'm just skipping the rest of this. I already told you my plan is just basic practice quizzes for retention, so I'm not going to engage with these other lessons right now.

options.A: Prompt the student to apply the learning principle via a cue to examine the tasks and resources provided in the LMS, and to describe in writing the resources appropriate for each objective.
options.B: Incorporate a variety of media and interactive tools (such as videos and interactive activities) within the training module to move beyond traditional text-based instruction during the introductory algebra course.
options.C: Restrict viewership of the student's open-ended prompt responses to only class members and the instructor to create a 'safe space' within the LMS during the training module.
options.D: Implement small-group skills practice for approximately 20 minutes daily, including computer-assisted instruction using the LMS, algebra fact activities, and a review consisting of 2 minutes to answer 15 practiced algebra facts.
